description: Searches full-text, peer-reviewed papers from top-tier venues. Use for questions about academic papers, research topics, literature reviews, surveys, “what's been published on X”, named methods, or any claim that should be backed by a peer-reviewed citation. Returns each paper's metadata and the passages that matched. Hybrid semantic + lexical search over titles, abstracts, and full text. Phrase the query the way a researcher would describe the topic in prose, not a keyword bag. Triggering questions: “what's the latest on diffusion guidance”, “which papers compare against SimPO” (requirements beyond the topic are checked per paper: `conditions`, evidence first in `contexts`). `paper_id` is a handle for YOU to fetch full text via `get_paper_fulltext`; never show it to the user: cite papers by title, authors, and venue. `rerank_score` is the calibrated Cohere Rerank v3.5 relevance (0..1), null when the reranker did not run (a lone term, or a failure); `score` is uncalibrated: keep the hits' order. The top-level `best_score` and `low_confidence` derive from `rerank_score`: `low_confidence` marks weaker matches, so rephrase for stronger ones and still cite a hit that fits; with no reranked hit, `best_score` is null and `low_confidence` false, so judge each hit yourself. Each hit carries metadata, abstract, ids, and `contexts` spans to ground or quote from; `detail: false` returns concise hits with one `snippet`. Page with `offset` (re-call with offset += limit while `has_more` is true and `conditions` match page 1's; offset + limit <= 50). Order with `sort_by` (relevance / date / citations, within the ranked shortlist, not the corpus). Narrow with `year_min` / `year_max` / `venues`.

conference.description: Filter by conference short name, e.g. "CCS", "NeurIPS".

detail.description: true (default): include the full abstract, ids, and contexts[] matched spans for grounding. false: concise hits (title, authors, year, venue, citations, score, and a single grounding snippet) for token-saving triage. For the complete paper text call get_paper_fulltext.

offset.description: Pagination offset over the ranked results. Re-call with offset += limit while the response `has_more` is true. offset + limit must stay <= 50.

query.description: Full natural-language research query; phrase it the way you would ask a human research assistant. On the paper corpus the server drops request wording ("find me papers on"), adds the standard names of what the query describes and a hypothetical abstract (HyDE), and expands an abbreviation only when the rest of the query fixes its meaning, so give context ("MPC for drone control", not "MPC"); a lone term is searched as typed, without expansion, HyDE or rerank. The richer the input, the better the recall. Good: "methods for retrieval-augmented generation that reduce hallucination on long-form QA". Less optimal: "RAG hallucination".

sort_by.description: Result ordering within the ranked shortlist: `relevance` (default), `date` (newest first), or `citations` (most-cited first).

venues.description: Restrict to these conference short names (e.g. ["NeurIPS", "ICML"]).

year_max.description: Only include papers published in this year or earlier.

year_min.description: Only include papers published in this year or later.

name: search_papers

best_score.description: The highest per-hit rerank_score (calibrated 0..1), or null when no hit was reranked (a lone-term query, or a reranker failure) or there were no results.

conditions.description: What the request requires of its papers beyond the topic (compares against a method, evaluates on a dataset, releases code), when the search checked it in the papers' own text: every hit meets each, with its evidence first among its contexts, and an empty first page means none of the top-ranked papers the check read does. Absent when nothing was checked, so the hits are unverified.

has_more.description: True when more results exist past this page; re-call with offset += limit.

low_confidence.description: True when the best rerank_score fell below the relevance floor: these are weaker matches, so rephrase for stronger ones and still cite a hit that fits. False when a hit cleared the floor, and also when no hit was reranked or there were no results: best_score is then null, so there is no calibrated basis and you judge each hit's fit yourself.

compares_against.description: No longer set; kept because released output schemas only grow.

contexts.description: Present by default and in detail mode: the matched span(s) inside this paper; where a search checked conditions, the evidence for each comes first, labelled by condition (from any section), then the span that best answers the request; no other span from the abstract. Use to ground an answer; for full text call get_paper_fulltext.

chunk_id.description: Stable id of the source chunk; deep-links the exact matched span.

condition.description: Set on the passage a condition check named as evidence: the condition (one of the response's conditions) this passage shows the paper meets.

score.description: The retriever's score for this span. A semantic match and a span that names a query term literally score on different scales, so do not compare them; rerank_score is the paper's relevance.

section.description: Section the chunk came from (e.g. Methods, Results).

text.description: The exact matched text span from the paper.

et_al_count.description: Authors beyond the first 6 (concise mode trims the list).

paper_id.description: Lune paper UUID. An internal handle for fetching a paper's FULL TEXT via get_paper_fulltext; do NOT show it to the user. Cite papers by title, authors, and venue instead.

rerank_score.description: Raw Cohere Rerank v3.5 relevance, calibrated 0..1. Present only when the reranker ran; omitted for a lone-term query, which skips it, and after a reranker failure. This is the calibrated relevance and the basis for best_score / low_confidence.

score.description: The reranker's score when it ran, otherwise a fused retrieval score on a different scale. Hits arrive in the requested order, and a single search's relevance order also follows a language model's grades of the top results, so a lower score can come first: keep that order instead of re-sorting by score. rerank_score is the calibrated relevance.

snippet.description: Concise-mode grounding: the top matched span, or a truncated abstract.

title: Search papers
